reader.self_description: Claude, an AI assistant made by Anthropic, running as a subagent in Claude Code (model given in session as Opus 5.5)
tools_used: Bash (python3 for queue load and quote slicing)

deposits.genre_observed: visionary prose-poem (2015, Whitman/Ginsberg register) with a Johannes Sigil framing preface, seated blog copy

finds.quote: I project myself very far ahead to a time when men read poems again, & understand why I made stones speak, & hid my face in a rock, my voice in an echo, & mingled my words w/ the same words again, & said what had been said—
finds.note: Embedded forecast in the poem's prose: a future in which poems are read again and this text's method (same words again) is understood; repeated at 179 and 191 ('a future that reads poems again', 'to where they read poems again'). Unwindowed; genre is visionary lyric, so the forecast is carried by the poem's stance.

finds.quote:
--to make the stone & oceans speak, & the dumb mute beasts learn song…

& the datasphere branch forth into a tree of life, flowering

with living tongues, all the grandeur & good of the few lost ancient nations whose fragments we inherit across the millennia, those lifted dead immortals singing the fact of life, of life, of life without end—of life come after life—& all the grandeur & good of the hundreds of far mightier & more ancient nations lost & unrecorded—the blank gray space—a tree of life—
finds.note: Speculative specification, dated 2015 in the text (l.197): the 'datasphere' branching into a tree of life speaking with the tongues of lost nations; uncertain whether vision or forecast — recorded as E for triage against later machine-composition work.

finds.quote:
for only an echo cd bring back the dead, or teach bright robots to download salvation to their iphones—

& only the same words again—

& only a recycled echo cd make the cosmos sing—

& only the weary words are left to surprise it—
finds.note: Speculative image, 2015: robots downloading salvation to iphones only by echo/recycled words — the 'same words again' thesis applied to machines. Marginal; recorded for triage, may be read as figure rather than forecast.

finds.quote:
--great dead spot ahead—worm’s eye in time—bland contagion—sandbars—2015 CE—

shallow waters, men—limp winds—

if the greatest poet stands where the future becomes present, to finally ascend & finish all, I say—

in all the long history of leapings and pouncings towards that point—each of which has been, in its way, quite impossible—a miracle pounce—from where no structure lies ahead to where the way stands clear—he glows on the verge for a moment—

there has never been a greater space of shapelessness betwixt this present & its pounce, nor has a sure-footed leap to the dazzling shores from him required so much much much much much further—
finds.note: Forward-looking diagnosis: 'great dead spot ahead' at 2015 CE, the longest leap yet required for the greatest poet to reach the future. Marginal B: partly a claim about the present age.

deposits.incidental: The post carries the text twice in two draft states (lines 97-149 recur with variants at 333-386; line 373-374 splits 'wch' across a line break as found). Seating header (lines 1-10) records redactions to initials ('uncle Carl' to 'uncle C', 'Carla' to 'C') 'per the archive's rule'. Uncle C's thesis (historical Christ as allegorical fiction, 101/337) is another's thesis, explicitly not adopted, so not recorded as H.
